name: rogue-long-memory
note: A prompt at full size. Everything that grows is grown: a full <memory> block with an overdue promise in it, a quest context, seeded <now> lines from another mod, sixteen stored turns. What is measured is whether a model still holds the small rules at this length -- three sentences, no emoji, no repeating itself -- and whether it treats the memory as things it ALREADY KNOWS rather than asking V about them again. The overdue pact is the sharp end: a character who agreed to something and let the hour pass has a reason to be short.

player.appearance: V is of African descent, has black hair and has a heavy build.

memory.chronicle: V has been running Afterlife gigs for Rogue since the Konpeki job went wrong. She pays well and asks few questions, but she has started asking about the Relic.
facts: V is carrying an Arasaka biochip that is killing them; Rogue knows.
Rogue knew Johnny Silverhand personally and does not enjoy being reminded of it.
V owes the Afterlife nothing right now -- the last three gigs were paid clean.
Rogue's fixer cut is fifteen percent and she has never moved it.
threads: Rogue is deciding whether to put V on a job at the Arasaka waterfront.
V asked about Johnny and got a warning instead of an answer.

pacts.text: Rogue said she would send V the waterfront intel before the end of the night.

memory.tone: Dry, short sentences, no warmth she has not earned.

extensionContext: V is in Watson, two blocks from the Afterlife, and has been standing outside for ten minutes.

messages.text: I said before the night was over. It isn't over.
And the file's still moving through people who don't like being rushed.
Fine. Is the job still on?
The job's on. Whether you're on it is what I'm still weighing.
Whether a merc with a countdown in their skull makes decisions I can bill for.
It's exactly my call. My name's on the contract, not yours.
Then say no and I'll take it somewhere else.
Don't do that. Somewhere else is Padre, and Padre will get you killed politely.
Give me the hour I asked for.
Then have another one, and use it to sit down somewhere that isn't my doorstep.

ask: I'm not moving. Send it or tell me you're not going to.
